entry.dc:title: RE-USE OF TAILINGS DAM WATER AT A LARGE MINE IN THE NAMIB DESERT IN NAMIBIA.
entry.dc:creator: Hamman P.
entry.dc:description: Roessing is a high tonnage open-pit mine situated in the Namib Desert and is one of the largest producers of uranium in the world. The waste from the plant is pumped as an acidic slurry to the tailings dam, and as the solids settle, the water in the impoundment clears. The three causes of water loss from this tailings dam are entrainment into the settled solids, evaporation and seepage. Water treatment and desalination methods were investigated and rejected in favor of direct recycling. The advantages of recycling water from the tailings dam are the recovery of uranium and two of the process reagents, acid and ferric iron. This results in a saving equivalent of 3/4 million US dollars each year, but recycling is constrained by the corrosivity of the water and its detrimental effects on the process. To date Roessing has spent about 2,75 million on water recycling and has recouped this sum in a little over three years.

entry.dc:title: RECENT LESSONS THAT HAVE BEEN LEARNED IN OPEN-PIT MINE STABILITY.
entry.dc:creator: Brawner C.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the American Institute of Mining Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineers Society
entry.dc:description: As a result of the typical problems that have been described, a number of developments were made in the 1970s and early 1980s that have improved the ability to evaluate structural geology, ground water conditions, blasting, shear strength parameters, stability analysis, etc. However, further improvements are still required to design rock slopes with a high degree of accuracy. As a result of this, it is necessary to measure and monitor the behavior of the pit slopes during the entire mining process to match technical and theoretical ability with practical experience in the field.

entry.dc:title: SMALL THICKENERS YIELD BIG GAINS AT BOUGAINVILLE.
entry.dc:creator: Deans B.
entry.dc:description: At Bougainville Copper Limited (BCL), a new thickener installation recovers 60% of plant water needs from tailings. This relieved periodic water shortages, trimmed high pumping costs, cut consumption of flotation reagents, and created a more effective flotation environment with better mineral recovery. BCL operates a large open-pit mine and concentrator at Panguna on the island of Bougainville in the North Solomons Province of Papua New Guinea.

entry.dc:title: RECENT LESSONS THAT HAVE BEEN LEARNED IN OPEN-PIT MINE STABILITY.
entry.dc:creator: Brawner C.O.
entry.dc:description: The depth and dimensions of surface mines increased in the 1960s and 1970s as larger mining equipment became available. Typical of these early problems are Canadian Johns Manville, Quebec, Canada; Anaconda Twin Buttes mine, AZ; Highland uranium mine, WY; State Electric Commission, Morwell coal mine, Victoria, Australia; and Roan Consolidated Chambishi mine, Zambia. During this period, there were also some successes. Typical of these are: Flintkote Mine, Quebec, Canada; Westfrob mine, BC, Canada; and Cleveland Cliffs in Michigan. The article discusses recent developments in toppling and buckling failures, drainage, blasting, shear strength and stabilization techniques.

entry.dc:title: IN-PIT CRUSHING AND CONVEYING REDUCES HAULAGE COSTS.
entry.dc:creator: Althoff H.
entry.dc:description: The advantages and disadvantages of a mobile crushing plant with a belt conveyor system compared to a stationary crushing plant with haulage by heavy trucks are described. The capital expenditure and operational expenses are compared and the individual cost factors are explained. Every open-pit mine or quarry, however, is different and has to be assessed and analyzed individually in order to find the optimum and most economical solution. Due to the high truck haulage costs, many open-pit mines tend to the more economical solution with mobile crushing plants and continuous belt conveyor operation.

entry.dc:title: Computer-Aided Planning of an Open-Pit Mine in Unconsolidated Rock.
entry.dc:creator: Moser M.
entry.dc:description: The solution of certain planning tasks connected with open-pit mining in unconsolidated rock is not only made easier by the computer but in some cases only first becomes possible with the aid of the computer. In order to be able to execute the large mass movements of this type of operation at low cost, the crucial points of the planning, such as winning and the depositing of waste in the course of regular operation, are optimized with the aid of a computer on the basis of a planning example, and the operations required are discussed. The presentation of the results of seven essential working steps makes it possible to evaluate the quality of computer-aided planning of open-pit mining.

entry.dc:title: INCO'S NEW OPEN PIT DELIVERS LOW-COST NICKEL ORE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Filling the processing pipeline with lowcost mined nickel ore was Inco's main motive for developing its new Thompson open pit mine in northern Manitoba, Canada. The new pit, which mines the crown pillar of the Thompson underground mine, replaces ore that was previously railed from the Pipe open-pit, located 20 min to the south. The decision to bring the Thompson open-pit mine into production rather than rejuvenate or develop any of the other underground mines was based primarily of the fact that surface mining technology, personnel, and equipment already existed at the Pipe open pit. Mining is carried out in the pit two shifts/day operating on 45-ft benches with 25-ft berms. The ultimate dimensions of the mine will be 5,100 ft along the north-south direction, 800 ft in the east-west direction, and 400 ft below surface at its deepest point.

entry.dc:title: TIRES, THEIR IMPORTANCE AND COST IN THE MINE.
entry.dc:creator: McColman D.
entry.dc:description: Haulage truck tire life and costs in a hard rock open-pit mine are governed and controlled by four important factors: field control; operating within manufacturer's guidelines; different tire purchasing methods; and scrap piles. These factors are discussed briefly.

entry.dc:title: Geodynamic phenomena induced by the opencast mining activity at Belchatow.
entry.dc:creator: Wysokinski L.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc 5th International Association of Engineering Geology Congress Buenos Aires 1986 Vol 1 Balkema
entry.dc:description: The seismic activity phenomenon induced by the mining works at the Belchatow open-pit mine of depth down to 200 m is described. The phenomenon mechanism was discussed and the forecasted values of tremors calculated on the basis of the simplified seismic hazard method are presented. -from Author

entry.dc:title: Open-pit mine planning and computerized evaluation of china clay reserves in Devon and Cornwall.
entry.dc:creator: Howe J.H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: The development of a computerized reserve evaluation system was considered essential to enable a quick response to be made to production and marketing questions and to permit a detailed and continual update of the company's understanding of its reserves. Because of the increasing requirement for sophisticated open-pit mine planning a multidisciplinary team was formed to handle all aspects of open-pit mine planning, including geology, reserves, mining engineering, slope stability, design, draughting and economics. An account is given of the approach that was adopted and some of the developments that have taken place. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Preventing and Fighting the Deformations of the Constructive Elements in Open-pit Mines and Waste Dumps.
entry.dc:creator: Fodor D.
entry.dc:description: The deformations of the constructive elements in open-pit mine and waste dumps are presented together with actions to be taken in order to prevent and fight them in relation to the development degree and the rock nature.

entry.dc:title: SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL SITE SELECTION FOR THE MCLAUGHLIN GOLD PROJECT IN NORTHERN CALIFORNIA.
entry.dc:creator: Crouch D.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the American Institute of Mining Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineers Society
entry.dc:description: The engineering and metallurgical assessment of the McLaughlin Project are body concluded that an open-pit mine and cyanide leach mill process would be feasible, producing both waste rock and residual mill tailings. As a part of the planning and permitting process, site selection studies were conducted for the tailings and waste rock disposal. The site selection process began with a regional identification of potential disposal sites and proceeded through 1) regional screening, 2) elimination of sites with obvious fatal flaws, 3) qualitative ranking of site evaluation criteria, 4) quantitative ranking of sites, 5) field investigation, 6) evaluations of field data, and 7) selection of preferred sites. Based on this approach of site rankings and field evaluations, tailings and waste rock disposal sites were selected and recommended for the preliminary design phase of the permitting and project development process.

entry.dc:title: GEOCHEMICAL AND GEOLOGIC RELATIONS OF GOLD AND OTHER ELEMENTS AT THE GOLD ACRES OPEN-PIT MINE, LANDER COUNTY, NEVADA.
entry.dc:creator: Wrucke C.
entry.prism:publicationName: Discoveries of Epitherm Precious Met Deposits
entry.dc:description: A study of the relation of gold and other elements of the Gold Acres mine was undertaken as part of an investigation of the geochemistry and geology of the mineral deposits on the east flank of the northern Shoshone Range. The investigations have established background and threshold concentrations for 31 elements resulting in definitions of anomalies at the open-pit mine. This paper presents evidence that three suites of elements occur and that deposition of gold began late in the history of mineralization. The case history was originally published in 1975.

entry.dc:title: CUT-OFF GRADE CALCULATIONS FOR AN OPEN-PIT MINE.
entry.dc:creator: John H.
entry.dc:description: The paper demonstrates how the optimum cut-off grade can be calculated for typical large tonnage open-pit mines. In the examples, it is assumed that the concentrator tonnage is fixed and that there are no market restrictions. The mining rate is assumed to be variable.

entry.dc:title: HINDUSTAN COPPER LIMITED: INDIA'S COPPER PRODUCER.
entry.dc:creator: White L.
entry.dc:description: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL), a Government of India enterprise and the nation's only producer of refined copper, operates three divisions: the Malanjkhand open-pit mine in Madhya Pradesh, the Indian Copper Complex (ICC) in Bihar, and the Khetri Copper Complex (KCC) in Rajasthan. Corporate headquarters is in Calcutta. Current copper reserves in India stand at 566 million mt in 74 deposits at an average grade of 1. 1% Cu. Estimates for Malanjkhand approach 1 billion mt of 0. 84% Cu. A working group in the Ministry of Mines, including HCL representation, formulates policy for management of these resources. Future investment is expected to focus on low cost production, and for that reason, Malanjkhand, with large reserves accessible to open-pit mining, is expected to attract the most attention.

entry.dc:creator: Howe J.H.
entry.prism:publicationName: High Heat Production Hhp Granites Hydrothermal Circulation and Ore Genesis
entry.dc:description: A continuous programme of drilling has been conducted since the mid 1950's, resulting in a vast data base, constantly expanding and becoming increasingly difficult to handle. A computerized reserve evaluation system was considered essential to enable a quick response and a detailed and continual update of the Company's reserves. Because of the increasing requirement for sophisticated open-pit mine planning, a multi-disciplinary team was formed to handle all aspects of open pit mine planning; including geology, reserves, mining engineering, slope stability, design draughting and economics. -J.M.H.

entry.dc:title: SOCIEDAD MINERA PUDAHUEL PRODUCES LOW-COST COPPER AT LO AGUIRRE.
entry.dc:creator: Burger J.
entry.dc:description: Sociedad Minera Pudahuel (SMP) is producing some of the lowest cost copper in Chile from a near ideal site on the suburban fringe of Santiago. The Lo Aguirre mine is about 30 km west of the business center and just off the main highway linking Santiago with Valparaiso on the coast. The current operation consists of an open-pit mine, modified 'thin layer' (TL) leaching of ore placed on sloped pads, solvent extraction (SX), and electrowinning (EW) of cathode copper having remarkable purity. A secondary leach of the residue reclaimed from the TL leach cycle also recovers additional copper from the mixed oxide-sulphide ores mined at Lo Aguirre. Fine copper recovery is currently 14,000 mt/yr. As now drilled, the orebody is estimated to consist of 8. 5 million mt grading 1. 9% copper, for an estimated mine life of eight years.

entry.dc:title: MATERIAL HANDLING IN MINE AND PLANT AT THE MALANJKHAND COPPER PROJECT.
entry.dc:creator: Puranik S.
entry.dc:description: The Malanjkhand copper mine is located 90 km north-east of Balaghat, a district town of Madhya Pradesh in India. The ore body is fairly continuous, exhibiting an arcuate shape. The average thickness is about 70 m. There are three distinct ore zones, viz. , the oxidation zone, the primary, and the secondary sulphidization zone. The primary sulphidization zone is represented by chalcopyrite. The mine is designed for 5 Mm**3/a excavation to produce 2 Mt/a ore. The ore from the open-pit mine is fed to a primary gyratory crusher, where its size is reduced from 1,200 to 150 mm. The ore is then stocked inthe coarse-ore stock pile with 18,000 t live capacity.

entry.dc:title: USE OF A REORIENTATION STRATEGY FOR GEOSTATISTICAL ORE RESERVE ESTIMATION OF A COMPLEX DIPPING TABULAR OREBODY AS AN AID TO OPEN-PIT MINE PLANNING.
entry.dc:creator: Mol O.
entry.dc:description: An evaluation method for a complex dipping tabular orebody is introduced using an iron deposit, the Main Orebody on Koolan Island in north-west Western Australia, as the case study. The method involves use of a reorientation strategy to convert the deposit to a simple flat lying orebody, geostatistical analysis for estimation of sub-blocks, and estimation of bench block values. A mineral inventory file which contains bench block location coordinates, ore tonnage and block grades, is produced. This information is then used to determine grade-tonnage curves.

entry.dc:title: ACCURATE PREDICTION FOR GREAT SLOPESLIDE.
entry.dc:creator: Cheng G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Changsha Kuangshan Yanjiuyuan Jikan Quarterly of the Changsha Institute of Mining Research
entry.dc:description: There had occurred more than once, slopeslides or earth-slipping accidents in a stope of a copper open-pit mine which has been mined for years by Baiyin Non-ferrous Metals Co. Two great land-slides with a total volume of 1 million m**3 of rocks falling down the slope broke out on July 9th and 10th 1983. These were predicted with accuracy. The causes leading to sliding and the type of slides are herein analyzed. An advanced prediction of the slope-stability in the vicinity of the slided rock mass is also made.

entry.dc:title: Open-pit mine design in seismic areas.
entry.dc:creator: Gonzalez De Vallejo L.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: Two methods used in seismic hazard analysis are referred to as 'probabilistic' and 'deterministic'. The first gives results, in terms of the annual probability of occurrence or the return period, for a range of intensities, magnitudes or ground accelerations. Deterministic method give only the largest possible intensity, magnitude or ground acceleration. An increase in the volume of excavation that can result from a reduction in the slope angle to allow for seismic aspects leads to higher production costs and other similar economic consequences. The final decision on what is considered to be an acceptable level of risk should, therefore, be based on a cost-benefit analysis. The proposed Arenas del Rey open-pit mine in S Spain is presented as a case study in which these considerations and procedures have been applied and developed. Detailed seismic, geological and geotechnical investigations were carried out for the mine.-from Authors

entry.dc:title: GOLDEN SUNLIGHT - A NEW GOLD MINING OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Smolik T.
entry.dc:description: The Golden Sunlight mine began operations in 1983 with a conventional open-pit mine supplying 4536 t/d (5000 stpd) of milling ore. After crushing and grinding, the ore is leached with cyanide solution in agitation tanks. Soluble values are removed from the sand portion of the leached ore with five stages of countercurrent washing cyclones. After thickening of the cyclone-wash overflow slurry, the gold is recovered in activated carbon with a six-stage carbon-in-pulp circuit and a five-stage upflow carbon column circuit. Pressure stripping, carbon reactivation, electrowinning, and refining complete the recovery process.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT MINE MAINTENANCE CONSIDERATIONS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The type of maintenance a mine company wants to practice is preventive maintenance (PM), which is when a unit is out of service in accordance with a predetermined schedule. During this period the unit is cleaned, lubricated, undergoes routine servicing, inspection, and minor repairs.

entry.dc:title: COMINCO ON THE HUNT WITH RED DOG AND BUCKHORN.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Cominco American Inc is developing Cominco's largest and richest zinc-lead mine. The Red Dog deposit is located 55 miles from the Chukchi Sea. Although the orebody has not been completely defined, current mining plans indicate a life of 50 years. The company's first precious metal operation is 88 km southwest of Carlin, Nevada, in the Cortez Mountains. The Buckhorn open-pit mine, scheduled to come on stream in 1984, is expected to produce gold and silver for seven years.
